title: Quickstart templates (RAG + agents) — Kickoff notes
content:
Doc is working notes (messy). Captured live during kickoff + a couple follow-ups.

Meeting
- Date/time: 2025-11-14 10:00–11:00 PT
- Organizer: Talia Benson
- Where: Zoom + #devex

Attendees
- DX: Alex Martinez (exec sponsor), Talia Benson (PgM)
- SDK: Monica Patel (lead), Ibrahim Khan (TL)
- Templates: Dana Lo (TS template lead)
- Docs: Elliot Price (docs lead), Wei Chen (quickstart owner)
- Platform/Telemetry: Logan Wright (lead), Allison Grant (standards)
- Security: Naomi Feldman (product security stakeholder)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE), (Rafael Mendes optional - couldn’t make this one)
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Marissa Cole (Console/rollouts)
- Support insights: Dev Patel (joined for 15 min)

Goal of kickoff (Alex)
- “Time to first success” < 15 minutes. “Production shape” from day one. Reduce tickets.
- IMPORTANT: do NOT teach unsafe patterns as the ‘happy path’.

Problem statement / why now
- Support keeps seeing same issues:
  - missing timeouts => hung requests / workers
  - 429 handling => loops / thundering herd
  - streaming disconnects behind proxies
  - unclear env vars, mis-set regions/models
  - logs too noisy + missing request_id
  - no tracing so Console looks empty / hard to debug

Scope (v1)
Templates to ship
1) RAG service + ingestion pipeline
   - default backend: pick 1 vector DB (TBD) + adapter interface
   - include ingestion worker + chunking defaults + doc format guardrails
2) Agent-style orchestration w/ tool calling
   - tool allow-list by default
   - per-tool timeouts + output schema validation
   - structured output path (json schema)
3) Combined RAG + agent
   - retrieval as tool + planner/executor-ish flow
   - basic prompt injection guardrails (don’t overclaim “secure”, but show patterns)

Languages
- Must: Python + TypeScript
- Nice-to-have: a small Go “advisor pass” (Mateusz to sanity-check patterns, not necessarily ship v1)

Deployment shapes
- Local dev (uv/poetry or npm) + .env
- Containerized (Docker Compose) with health checks
- Minimal k8s manifests (later phase, but align early so we don’t paint ourselves into a corner)

Telemetry + “production shape” (Logan / Allison / Sean)
- Standard contract for logs/metrics/trace attrs. Need consistency across Python/TS.
- Must include correlation IDs:
  - request_id (our own + echo Redwood header if present)
  - tenant_id (if app supports it; should be optional but supported)
  - route/model tags for breakdown
- Metrics baseline:
  - request latency (p50/p95) + streaming time-to-first-token
  - error count by class (timeout / 429 / upstream / validation)
  - token usage + cost (as close as we can get; at least “tokens_in/tokens_out”)
- Traces:
  - include spans: “redwood.generate”, “retrieval.query”, “tool.<name>”, “ingestion.chunk”, etc.

Safe defaults (Naomi / Sean)
- Must haves:
  - timeouts everywhere (HTTP client + tool calls)
  - retries w/ jittered exponential backoff (but not for all errors)
  - clear 429 behavior (respect Retry-After if present; max attempts)
  - idempotency guidance for non-streaming
  - do not log prompts/user content by default (PII). Provide a debug flag w/ warnings.
  - secrets: .env for local only; no committing; mention key rotation
  - input validation + size limits (upload/doc size; max tokens)

What “good” looks like (draft success metrics)
- TTFX: first successful run locally in < 15 minutes following README
- Deploy: < 60 minutes to a managed environment (we can define “managed” = basic k8s or container host)
- Support: decrease in top 5 onboarding ticket categories (Dev to provide baseline)
- Observability: dashboards light up without users hand-wiring OTel

Key decisions made (tentative)
- Repo approach: single “redwood-quickstarts” monorepo w/ shared libs (config loader, telemetry helpers)
- Provide a stable env var contract shared across templates/languages
- OTel instrumentation is part of the template, not an optional appendix
- Default logging is structured JSON + correlation fields; minimal verbosity by default

Open questions (needs follow-up)
1) Default vector DB for v1?
   - Candidates mentioned: Postgres + pgvector vs. (managed) Pinecone vs. local Qdrant.
   - Constraints:
     - should work locally without account creation
     - should be common enough for real users
     - should not complicate security posture
   - Action: Dana + Monica propose 1 primary + 1 “supported alt” by 11/22.

2) Token usage/cost attribution source of truth in templates
   - Can we reliably capture tokens via SDK response fields?
   - If Hosted API returns token usage, use it. If not, we may need an approximation.
   - Nadia to confirm fields + recommended metric names.

3) Request ID propagation
   - Do we get a request_id header back consistently? (Henry had previous notes)
   - Need to join traces between customer app + Redwood upstream.
   - Action: Logan to confirm required header propagation behavior; may require small API tweak.

4) Streaming reconnect behavior
   - How aggressive should reconnect be? When to stop and surface error?
   - Support reports proxies dropping idle streams.
   - Monica/Ibrahim to propose defaults; Sean to review for “no thundering herd”.

5) Security claims / language in docs
   - Naomi: avoid implying templates make you “compliant” or “secure by default” universally.
   - Need clear guidance: what we do, what customers must do.
   - Elliot/Wei to draft language; Naomi to review.

6) Agent/tool safety
   - How much do we standardize tool schema validation?
   - JSON schema libraries differ across languages.
   - Need a simple example that doesn’t require a framework.

Risks / watchouts
- Scope creep: “support every backend” will kill timeline. Must start opinionated.
- Telemetry cardinality: tags like user_id/document_id can explode. Must have guidelines.
- Drift between docs and repos (snippets rot) — need automation early.
- CI reliability: smoke tests against staging may flake (rate limits, transient networking).
- “Local dev friction”: dependency installs, OS-specific issues. Keep prerequisites minimal.

Action items (initial)
- Talia:
  - create Linear project + initial tickets + timeline checkpoint (by 11/18)
  - schedule weekly 30 min check-in + biweekly stakeholder review
- Monica/Ibrahim:
  - draft retry/timeout/streaming helper spec (SDK-side) (by 11/25)
- Dana:
  - propose TS template structure + config layering approach (by 11/22)
- Elliot/Wei:
  - outline docs-site IA for templates + “production checklist” page (by 11/26)
- Logan/Allison:
  - first draft telemetry contract (metrics/log fields/trace attrs) + cardinality notes (by 11/27)
- Sean:
  - recommended alert thresholds for dashboards defaults; avoid pager spam (by 12/02)
- Naomi:
  - quick pass on secrets + logging redaction guidance (by 12/02)
- Dev:
  - baseline: top onboarding ticket drivers + counts (last 90 days) (by 11/21)

Notes / random parking lot
- “Please don’t teach people to disable SSL verification” (yes this happens)
- Need a consistent error taxonomy for templates (ex: RW_ERR_TIMEOUT, RW_ERR_RATE_LIMIT, RW_ERR_UPSTREAM, RW_ERR_VALIDATION)
- Consider ‘/healthz’ + ‘/readyz’ endpoints for API templates; ingestion worker should have a simple “can connect to vector DB + Redwood” check.
- We should have a single place where env vars are documented + validated at boot.
- Put “how to rotate API key” and “what happens if key leaks” in README (brief, not scary)

Next meetings
- 2025-11-21: backend decision (vector DB + doc ingestion format)
- 2025-11-27: telemetry contract v0 review

Owner notes (Talia)
- Keep this project ‘tight’: v1 is 3 templates + observability pack + docs integration.
- Reconfirm launch gate with Product: what is “good enough” for Feb.
